title: Central-action identity and derived-invariant vanishing
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring on the coherent profinite site [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention], let $J$ be a topological group, and let $\mathcal A_R(J)$ consist of internal $R$-modules with an action of the condensed group $\underline J(S)=C(S,J)$ [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Let $\Gamma_J$ be the submodule of sections fixed after every profinite base change and let $R\Gamma_J$ be its ordinary total right derived functor [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with the action-category and derived-functor structures of [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus]. For $N\in\mathcal A_R(J)$ and $z\in J$ in the centre, let $z_N:N\to N$ be the equivariant endomorphism acting on sections over $S$ by the constant map $S\to J$ of value $z$. Then
$$R\Gamma_J(z_N[0])=\mathrm{id}_{R\Gamma_J(N[0])}.$$
If $z_N-\mathrm{id}_N$ is an isomorphism of action modules, then $R\Gamma_J(N[0])$ is a zero object of $D(\operatorname{Mod}_R)$. No triviality, finite-dimensionality, compactness or discreteness assumption on $N$ or $J$ is imposed.

proof.text: For every action module $M$, define $z_M(S)(m)=c_z\cdot m$, where $c_z:S\to J$ is constant. This is $R(S)$-linear and commutes with restrictions. For $g\in C(S,J)$, pointwise centrality gives $c_zg=gc_z$, hence $z_M(S)(g\cdot m)=g\cdot z_M(S)(m)$. Thus it is a morphism in the action category of [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Every equivariant $f:M\to M\prime$ satisfies $f z_M=z_{M\prime}f$ by its defining equivariance, also for all test sets. In particular these operators commute with any equivariant differential and augmentation.

proof.text: The input $N[0]$ is bounded below. By [lem-sfb-condensed-action-injective-infrastructure], choose an equivariant quasi-isomorphism $s:N[0]\to I^\bullet$ with $I^\bullet$ a bounded-below complex of injectives in $\mathcal A_R(J)$, which is K-injective. The same statement identifies $R\Gamma_J(N[0])$ with $\Gamma_J I^\bullet$ in the derived category via the invertible computation unit. Step 1 supplies the chain map $z_I$ with $z_I s=s z_N[0]$. No underlying-module injectivity or continuous-cochain comparison is used.

proof.text: By the fully fixed section condition of [def-sfb-condensed-action-module], a section $m\in\Gamma_J(I^q)(S)$ is fixed in particular for the identity base change $S\to S$ and the constant $c_z\in C(S,J)$. Thus $z_{I^q}(m)=m$. The invariants inclusion is injective on sections and its functor restricts equivariant maps, so $\Gamma_J(z_{I^q})$ is the identity in every degree. Consequently $\Gamma_J(z_I)$ is the identity chain map, not merely a map inducing identities on cohomology.

source.place: Paragraph (3), dense-lattice input: evaluate the normalized invariant-submodule condition at the constant central element; agent expansion

proof.text: Write $F=R\Gamma_J$, and let $Q_A,Q_R$ be localization from action complexes and module complexes. In [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] the computation unit $\eta:Q_R\Gamma_{J,K}\Rightarrow FQ_A$ is natural and $\eta_I$ is invertible. Hence $F(Q_Az_I)\eta_I=\eta_I Q_R(\Gamma_Jz_I)=\eta_I$, so $F(Q_Az_I)=1$. Applying $FQ_A$ to $z_I s=s z_N[0]$ now gives $F(Q_As)F(z_N[0])=F(Q_As)$. Since $s$ is a quasi-isomorphism, $F(Q_As)$ is invertible. Cancel it to obtain the required equality $F(z_N[0])=1$ in the ordinary derived category.

source.place: Tags 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined) and 070K (lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies); explicit naturality and cancellation with the universal computation unit

proof.text: Assume $u=z_N-1_N$ is invertible in the action category and set $X=R\Gamma_J(N[0])$. Additivity of the ordinary derived functor from [lem-sfb-condensed-action-injective-infrastructure] and step 4 give $R\Gamma_J(u[0])=R\Gamma_J(z_N[0])-1_X=0$. Functors preserve inverses, so this zero endomorphism is invertible; composing it with its inverse yields $1_X=0$. For every object $Y$, any $f:X\to Y$ satisfies $f=f1_X=0$, and any $h:Y\to X$ satisfies $h=1_Xh=0$. There is a zero morphism in each direction, so $X$ is both initial and terminal, hence a zero object.
